sources.title: Migración forzada y refugiados guatemaltecos en México: Relaciones transfronterizas e interculturalidad
sources.author: Joaquín Peña Piña; José Luis Francisco Mateo; Yaneth Candelaria López Méndez
sources.annotation: Read printed pp.104–107 and 118–125 of the actual 25-page article. The publisher identifies coauthor Francisco Mateo as of Akateko and K’anjob’al origin and a child of refugees. Focuses on the mixed San Marcos community, including settlement, education promoters and cross-border ties. Originally published July 2020; current version updated February 2022. Narrated land acquisition is not a present title ruling. Language-loss percentages and broad historical generalizations are not adopted.

sources.title: El estudio de la juventud como representación social en la población acateka de origen guatemalteco en Chiapas
sources.author: Verónica Ruiz Lagier
sources.annotation: Read printed pp.103–110 of the original nine-page article, including research context, three-community comparisons and attributed interviews. Fieldwork began in 2002, with a dated 2010 returnee interview. Studies La Gloria, San Francisco and Nueva Libertad; the author explicitly rejects uniform generalization. Older language terminology is not adopted as present classification. Personal experiences, gender expectations and changing practices do not establish current prevalence or a single community rule.

sources.title: La fotografía y el trabajo etnográfico. El caso de la comunidad akateka: La Gloria.
sources.author: Verónica Ruiz-Lagier
sources.annotation: Read the complete substantive publisher HTML, from introduction through conclusions, and checked original metadata; downloaded PDF, without claiming visual image analysis. A November 2021 visit adds new La Gloria memory/photography evidence to the author’s earlier work. Publisher dates publication March 6, 2024; SciELO’s later deposit date is not the original publication. Proposed museum/photo transfers are not confirmed complete. No ritual instructions, photographs or precise cultural sites are reproduced.

sources.title: The Maya Peoples of L.A.
sources.author: Emilia Sánchez González, interviewing Aurora Pedro and Genesis Ek
sources.publisher: J. Paul Getty Trust / Getty News
sources.annotation: Read the full October 10, 2022 original interview. Aurora Pedro is explicitly identified as Maya Akateko and Q’anjob’al; Genesis Ek has a separate Yucatan Maya background. Pedro recounts her family’s flight through Chiapas and advocates institutional language access. This is identified personal testimony, not a diaspora census or every family’s route. Broad introductory claims about ancient Maya language/script and group-wide arrival dates are not adopted.

proposedParagraphs.title: Building a community after refuge
proposedParagraphs.text: A study coauthored by José Luis Francisco Mateo, identified by the publisher as of Akateko and K’anjob’al origin and a child of refugees, follows families who chose to remain in Chiapas. It recounts repeated moves, work and collective efforts to obtain land before establishing San Marcos in La Trinitaria. Education promoters and continuing visits to relatives across the border also appear in the account. This is a particular mixed community’s history, rather than evidence that every Akateko family followed the same route or made the same choice.

proposedParagraphs.title: Young people, education and belonging
proposedParagraphs.text: Ruiz Lagier’s 2011 study compares young people in La Gloria, San Francisco and Nueva Libertad. Her interviews connect schooling, work, migration and family expectations with changing ideas about adulthood and gender. Young returnees can seek different choices while still asserting a Migueleño connection with San Miguel Acatán. The author compares public expectations with everyday practices, rather than treating them as identical. These dated accounts show negotiation within and across communities; they are neither a current survey nor instructions for how all Akateko people should live.

proposedParagraphs.title: Photographs, memory and who represents the community
proposedParagraphs.text: Returning to La Gloria in 2021, Ruiz-Lagier considered how earlier refugee photographs became part of remembering the community’s origins. Her 2024 article describes a local cultural promoter seeking photographs for community use and reflects on the different perspectives of residents, photographers and researchers. She also notes that religious participation had changed. This makes memory a continuing social process, rather than a single unchanging story. The article does not establish a completed museum or authorize copying its images; its account remains an attributed interpretation.

proposedParagraphs.title: One family’s route to Los Angeles
proposedParagraphs.text: In Getty’s 2022 interview, Aurora Pedro, identified as Maya Akateko and Q’anjob’al, recounts her family fleeing Guatemala to Chiapas in 1982 and later moving to Los Angeles, where she was born. She connects experiences of racism across borders with the work of building community. Speaking about CIELO’s advocacy, she calls for schools, hospitals and other public institutions to provide meaningful language access. Her family’s account makes one diaspora history visible without turning a dual identity, an organization’s work or an individual route into a description of all Akateko migrants.

countRecommendation.note: Four directly relevant works. The two Ruiz-Lagier publications are different studies with distinct youth/education versus new memory/photography evidence, not independent corroboration of every shared background claim. PDF, HTML and catalogue manifestations each count once. Broader regional refugee work and unread Prospera abstracts do not enter this minimum.

researchGaps: Add Akateko community-authored or directly focused accounts from Campeche and Quintana Roo; general Guatemalan refugee camp histories are not automatically Akateko histories.
The two Ruiz-Lagier studies share earlier fieldwork. Distinct topics and later observations do not make their repeated historical background independent confirmation.
Current demographics, language-use rates, present land title, educational outcomes and institutional program status are not established by these dated cases.
The youth study’s older terminology linking Akateko and K’anjob’al should be distinguished from current community naming and linguistic work reviewed by the language researcher.
Full Prospera education/gender manuscripts were not retrieved from publicly linked university repositories because downloads returned403. Abstracts are leads, not inspected substantive sources.

Getty’s general introduction includes language/script and broad historical claims not adopted here. The cited evidence is the attributed interview, with the two women’s distinct backgrounds preserved.
The2024 author reports a2021 event while several image captions say2022. No precise photographic capture date is inferred, and no visual or film analysis is claimed.

excludedOrSupporting.title: Los refugiados guatemaltecos y la frontera-frente de discriminación, explotación y desigualdad
excludedOrSupporting.author: Verónica Ruiz Lagier
excludedOrSupporting.inspectedScope: Read printed pp.47–48 and51–55 in actual eleven-page PDF.
excludedOrSupporting.reason: Valuable regional refugee/citizenship context, but the detailed personal/institutional cases principally concern other groups, including Q’anjob’al Nuevo Huixtán. Its Akateko relevance is broader context; kept outside the directly focused minimum.

integrationNotes: Read public nonrestricted material only; no people contact, site/data/build edits or publishing.

Community, nationality, citizenship, individual ethnicity and refugee/migrant experiences are related without being interchangeable identities. Akateko and K’anjob’al origins must remain separately named where the source identifies both.
No personal migration testimony is used to imply present immigration status; no minor’s route or name is reproduced in proposed prose.

No ceremonial instructions, visual assets, exact burial/cultural-site coordinates or local full-text cache files should be served. Linked documentary and older photographic works are not additional reviewed sources.
